subject: Post-demo pricing & capacity follow-up — dedicated options and unit economics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@finlytics.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & quick pricing questions (FinLytics)

Alex — great running through the GenSearch demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size a dedicated proposal that hits your cost targets.

Key asks (need answers to these to produce a dedicated reserved quote):
- Expected steady-state token volume: current baseline + projected ramp (tokens/day, or tokens/month)
- Target unit economics: what is your target $/1M tokens for a dedicated stack?
- Latency & throughput requirements: p50/p95 latency SLOs, and aggregate throughput target (tokens/sec)
- GPU preference (A100 80GB vs H100 vs other) or openness to guidance from us
- Budget range (monthly committed spend) and procurement timeline

We can run two scenarios: 1) 2x A100-80GB reserved, 2) 3x H100 reserved (higher perf) — and show tokens/$ per 1M for each. I’ll loop in Marissa to draft the SOW and preliminary cost sheet once you confirm volumes & budget range.

Attachments: I’ll include a placeholder estimate once we have numbers.

Next step: can you reply with the volumes/range and whether you prefer A100 or H100 guidance? Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

----
From: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & quick pricing questions (FinLytics)

Ben / Olga — thanks for the follow-up, appreciate the clear asks. Answers below:

1) Volumes (current and forecast)
- Current: ~6M tokens/day (search + enrichment during business hours)
- Q3 target (after rollout to EU customers): 20M tokens/day
- Q4 target: 45–50M tokens/day (national rollout + batch indexing windows)

2) Target unit economics
- We’re looking for something in the ballpark of $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens for committed capacity.
- For bursty, pay-as-you-go traffic we accept higher unit cost but want committed tiers to be in that band.

3) Latency & throughput SLOs
- p50 generation latency target: <150ms
- p95: <500ms
- Aggregate throughput target: ~100k tokens/sec during peak (expected short spikes), sustained throughput target: 15k–25k tokens/sec

4) GPU preference
- Open to guidance. We prefer a solution that nails p95 while keeping committed costs predictable. If H100 materially improves throughput/cost that’s preferred, but cost per month needs to stay in the budget range (see below).

5) Budget & timeline
- Monthly committed budget target: $25k–$45k depending on unit economics and SLA
- Procurement: aiming to finalize by end of July for Q3 rollout

Hope this helps — let me know if you want any of those numbers broken down by region (US vs EU). Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through cost scenarios.

— Alex
VP Product | FinLytics
alex.navarro@finlytics.com

----
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@finlytics.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap & quick pricing questions (FinLytics)

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Alex’s reply and adding my read. High level: FinLytics expects 45–50M tokens/day by Q4, target $/1M of $800–$1,200 for committed capacity, and peak brief spikes up to ~100k tokens/sec. They asked us for guidance on A100 vs H100 and need a proposal that fits a $25k–$45k/month committed window. Procurement by end of July.

Immediate asks for quoting team (Marissa):
- Provide two committed scenarios (monthly MSRP + committed discount):
  • Scenario A: Reserved 2x A100-80GB (expected to handle sustained 15k–25k tokens/sec, with autoscale burst to 60k tokens/sec) — show $/1M tokens and expected p95
  • Scenario B: Reserved 3x H100 (higher throughput, better for sustained and p95) — show $/1M tokens and expected p95
- Include buffer for EU region (assume +20% capacity) and show net monthly committed cost for US-only vs US+EU
- Include clear fallback plan if they hit sustained >50M/day (burst credits, on-demand pools)

Marissa — can you produce the quick estimate CSV and a one-page SOW draft that we can send to Alex? Ben, can you own the follow-up call scheduling and present scenario tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Solutions Operations | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: Redwood-Dedicated-Estimate-FinLytics.csv (placeholder), SOW-draft-FinLytics.pdf (placeholder)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@finlytics.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & quick pricing questions (FinLytics)

Alex — thanks for the detail, this is perfect. Next steps:
- We’ll get you two formal scenarios (A100 vs H100) with per-1M token math and projected p95 latency estimates by EOD Monday (attached CSV + one-pager SOW).
- If the numbers look good, propose a 45-minute pricing walkthrough the week of May 25 to go line-by-line and lock in a preferred reserved size.
- I’ll include cost impact for EU footprint (+20%) and a clear burst/on-demand fallback so you’re not exposed during rollout spikes.

Two quick clarifications before we prepare the quote:
1) For sustained 45–50M tokens/day, do you expect most of that to be distributed across 12 business hours or concentrated in 3–4 bigger windows? (impacts cache sizing and KV RAM needs)
2) Any compliance or data residency requirements beyond standard SOC2 / EU data locality we should add to the SOW?

I’ve attached a placeholder estimate and a short SOW draft for your internal review. If you’re available May 25–27, share a few times and I’ll send an invite.

Thanks again,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
